answer_1.quote: Our data consists of prompts from several categories (General, STEM, Coding and Multilingual)... We train dedicated Feedback and Edit models... which can be used at inference time to improve model responses to open-ended general-domain tasks.
answer_1.outputs: textual responses, free‑text feedback, edited responses

answer_2.quote: we measure the helpfulness of models ... using three popular metrics: AlpacaEval 2.0 Length Controlled, GPT-4‑Turbo MT Bench and Arena Hard.

answer_3.quote: MT Bench ... with GPT‑4‑Turbo (specifically GPT‑4‑0125‑Preview) as the judge... AlpacaEval ... sent to GPT‑4‑1106‑turbo evaluator... Arena Hard ... compared with responses from GPT‑4‑0314 using GPT‑4‑1106‑preview judge... we generate up to 16 responses ... choose the response that has the highest reward from Llama‑3.1‑70B‑Reward.

answer_4.quote: We also conduct a small‑scale human evaluation. We randomly identify 50 first‑turn prompts... ask 3 in‑house annotators to independently annotate each prompt (8 annotators in total) on whether they prefer a response from Llama‑3.1‑... or the same model with an optimally‑scaled Feedback‑Edit ITS system.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were asked to indicate which of two responses they preferred; preferences were aggregated across annotators.
